g.text: Make verification cheap, independent and repeatable
Sonar motivates independent checks; Capital One argues for lowering the cost of engineering rigor.

Supply intent, constraints, shared test fixtures and fast low-noise checks while work is generated. Keep deterministic checks for properties that can be asserted exactly. Another model’s agreement or a quick approval does not replace independent evidence of correctness.

Test interfaces, permissions, financial invariants and representative regressions. Inspect the current saved artifact after the last edit. Keep the evidence and the decision owner together; a check that can be bypassed or does not halt the relevant action is an incomplete gate.

Capture escaped failures, reconstruct their context and verify the repair against other work. The confidence product in Sonar’s talk is conceptual, and its code-size illustration is workload-specific. Neither supplies a calibrated assurance formula or a universal limit on agent-generated software.
Sources: Sonar · Capital One | Reviewed October 25, 2026
